analyst_view.overall: Bayern are still without Vincent Kompany, who is recovering from a viral inflammation of the brain membranes, so Aaron Danks leads the team again. Danks said Díaz, Gnabry, Musiala and Saibari remain out, Pavlovic is fit to start, and Alphonso Davies may be rested after a long run of midweek games. Mainz lost three games in a week. Urs Fischer wants his side to get back to basics, with 'running, duels, intensity, aggression', and he has to rebuild his back line without the suspended Posch and Mwene.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Mainz have conceded 17 in their last six, and with Posch and Mwene suspended Fischer has to bring in Stefan Bell or Rael Nakuzola at the back, which points up. Bayern are missing four attackers and Danks is managing workloads before the international break, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern should have most of the ball against a Mainz side focused on defending, and nothing in the news moves the corner figure either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Fischer has asked for aggression and hard duels, and local reports say Mainz plan to be 'eklig' (nasty to play against), with a reshuffled defence chasing Bayern's attackers. That points to more fouls and bookings than usual. Robert Schröder referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots. Bayern have scored 18 in their last six and face a weakened Mainz back line. Possible rotation (Davies may be rested) and the missing attackers stop us going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 shots on target. A makeshift Mainz defence should concede chances, but Bayern's thin front line and their tired legs after Tuesday's win at Atlético balance that out.
